text: The real build starts right here — connecting to exactly the tables Lesson 84's written scope actually needs, and genuinely nothing more than that, using the very same SQL Server connector Chapter 2 already walked you through.

Nine tables total, each one selected deliberately from the Navigator dialog rather than grabbed on impulse. Every single one traces directly back to one of Lesson 84's four requirements — resist the very real temptation to import the entire database just in case something turns out useful later, since a smaller, deliberate model stays easier to reason about at every later step of this project.

Import mode wins here for one genuinely specific reason: this particular project doesn't need real-time data at all, and Import mode gives you the fastest possible experience while you're actively building visuals across the lessons still ahead of you. Lesson 92 revisits this exact same choice once scheduled refresh comes back into the picture.

One real asymmetry worth remembering for good: cutting an unused column later on is genuinely cheap and easy, once you actually know for certain you don't need it. Discovering you never imported a column you actually needed is not cheap at all, and means reconnecting to the source all over again from scratch. When you're genuinely in doubt about a column, bring it in now rather than regret it later on.

All nine tables are loaded, and their row counts have been checked carefully for anything obviously wrong — no table sitting there completely empty, and every count looking genuinely plausible for a real warehouse this size. Lesson 86 is exactly where the real cleanup work actually begins, over in Power Query.
